title: The circuit can contain more than 100% gas
evidence: The headless probe at O2 6 L/min, air 0, dial 8%, after 30 simulated minutes reports O2 100.000% plus agent 7.904%: total 107.904%. O2 and agent are integrated and clamped independently.
impact: This violates a basic composition invariant within the visible control range. Any lesson relying on oxygen dilution or low-flow composition is suspect until the balance is corrected.
remedy: Track all species and total gas amount consistently, account for vapor addition and uptake, and enforce conservation tests rather than renormalizing an incorrect calculation at the display.

title: Three instantaneous shock clicks guarantee ROSC
evidence: pads, cpr and three shock actions at t=0 cause rhythm ROSC at the next 0.5-second tick. There is no minimum CPR interval, rhythm reassessment, charging state or shock-delivery prerequisite beyond the accumulated action count.
impact: The recovery reward contradicts the timing the text purports to teach. RCUK 2025 ordinarily specifies a shock followed by two minutes of CPR; its narrowly defined stacked-shock exception also has different counting for drug timing.
remedy: Implement an explicit arrest state machine, timed CPR cycles, reassessment and appropriate exceptional branches. Treat ROSC as a scenario outcome with declared assumptions, never an automatic three-click rule.

title: A reversed sequence can receive a perfect order score
evidence: Entering every critical action in reverse order at the same simulation time produces orderScore=1. buildDebrief compares first-action timestamps using >=, rather than reading the event log sequence.
impact: The assessment can reward the opposite of the intended algorithm. This invalidates the order score as evidence of learning.
remedy: Use monotonic event sequence numbers and a protocol dependency graph; support actions that may occur in parallel, required repeats and clinical exceptions. Re-test identical timestamps and rapid clicks.

title: A single MH action normalizes most vital signs while the trigger stays on
evidence: With only dantrolene selected, at 180 seconds the model reports sinus rhythm, HR 92, BP 124/72, SpO2 98 and EtCO2 42. Calling for help, stopping the trigger, TIVA and cooling remain unperformed. The dantrolene target branch overrides trigger state.
impact: Learners can infer that the other critical actions do not matter. This is a model-design failure, not a statement about a real patient response.
remedy: Have a clinician define the intended causal response to persistent triggers, incomplete treatment and recurrence; use a reviewed transition model or a coupled metabolic model within a declared domain.

title: There is no recorded named clinician approval
evidence: The executable registry has 201 entries: 156 sourced, 6 from-memory, 39 illustrative, and zero populated reviewedBy fields. Source status is not expert review or simulator validation.
impact: The project cannot substantiate a claim of clinically reviewed fidelity from this repository. Absence of a recorded reviewer does not prove nobody has ever looked at it informally.
remedy: Assign a clinical lead and qualified module reviewers; record identity, role, scope, version, date, corrections and unresolved limitations. Start with the workstation and one student scenario.

title: The main ventilator cannot be set like a ventilator
evidence: Vt=480 mL, RR=12, I:E=1:2 and PCV inspiratory pressure=8 are in DEFAULT_PARAMS, but the main settings panel exposes no controls for Vt, RR, I:E or PCV inspiratory pressure. The running DOM confirms six steppers: O2, air, vaporizer, PEEP/APL, R and C.
impact: Students cannot practice basic ventilation adjustments or compare pressure and volume control on their own terms. The core machine-learning promise is missing essential interaction.
remedy: Expose an authentic, labeled ventilation control panel, set-versus-measured values, units, pressure limit and inspiratory timing; keep an introductory mode with a smaller initial set.
basis: Source inspection plus current local DOM

title: The APL setting acts as an invented pressure source
evidence: In spontaneous mode pb is assigned APL, or 0.85 times APL, without a bag-volume pressure model. There is no squeeze action. The setting directly supplies the breathing baseline instead of acting as a pressure-relief threshold.
impact: This can teach that setting the APL generates pressure or CPAP by itself. The critical relationship between inflow, bag, leak, relief and patient effort is absent.
remedy: Model reservoir volume, manual bag compression, pressure-dependent APL outflow and patient muscle pressure. Separate spontaneous breathing, manual ventilation and turbine CPAP.

title: The bellows-leak fault does nothing to PCV mechanics
evidence: The probe gives 478 mL with and without the leak in PCV. In VCV the same flag changes 533 to 366 mL. leakFrac is only used in the VCV flow assignment, although the scene still indicates a leak.
impact: Mode-dependent fault handling is inconsistent. The PCV path silently omits the leak rather than simulating pressure compensation, leakage flow or limits.
remedy: Represent a leak as a pressure-dependent circuit path shared across modes. Test delivered and expired volume, leak flow and compensation limits for each architecture.

title: Gas exchange ignores the ventilation settings
evidence: At RR/Vt of 4/150, 12/450 and 30/900 the probe reports the same PaO2, 579.906 mmHg, and the same saturation. PaCO2 is hardcoded at 40. This is a static shunt calculation with an animated ventilation view.
impact: The UI invites changes whose expected gas-exchange consequences are not modeled. It can be useful for isolation anatomy, but not for predicting the physiology of hypoventilation.
remedy: Either couple alveolar ventilation, CO2, FRC and oxygen stores over time, or explicitly limit the screen to an equilibrium shunt illustration and remove misleading physiological controls/readouts.

title: Green perineural feedback does not require a visible needle tip
evidence: The positive note depends on proximity within nerve radius +2 mm and absence of the current collision message. It is selected before ultrasound needle visibility is computed, and has no visibility condition.
impact: A learner may receive an encouraging position cue while the needle is out of the beam. The caveat that the cue is educational helps, but the feedback still rewards an incomplete safety behavior.
remedy: Require a visible, localized tip and a reviewed sequence of checks for positive feedback; distinguish position illustration from acceptable procedural performance. Retain the uncertainty warning.

title: Needle injury disappears when the tip is moved away
evidence: Safety checks evaluate the current point. There is no persistent vessel/pleura/nerve injury state or path history in SonoLab. Withdrawing from a hazardous point clears the message; local anesthetic volume remains an independent slider.
impact: This teaches collision avoidance at one instant rather than consequences of puncture or unsafe injection. It must not be assessed as a procedure or complication-management simulation.
remedy: Record path crossings and injections as events, latch injuries with explicit scenario consequences, and separate exploration reset from clinical recovery.

title: The English interface declares safe extubation from TOF alone
evidence: thumbSafeToExtubate is just ratio >=0.9 and the English badge reads SAFE EXTUBATION >=0.90. The French wording is more conditional. The model has no airway patency, respiratory recovery or consciousness assessment.
impact: TOF recovery is one necessary neuromuscular condition, not a complete extubation decision. The manufacturer label separately requires adequate respiration and a patent airway [S2].
remedy: Change the badge to a narrowly scoped statement about measured neuromuscular recovery; present other extubation considerations in reviewed teaching content and never issue an overall safety verdict from this variable.

title: The sugammadex explanation contradicts the model compartment
evidence: The English and French success text locates encapsulation in the synaptic cleft, and the gold rings animate there. The numerical binding calculation instead operates on rocPlasma. This confuses complex formation and redistribution away from the junction.
impact: The visual mechanism and the implemented compartment teach different stories. The label describes complex formation that reduces NMBA available for junctional binding [S2]; the original population PK-PD paper describes plasma capture and the resulting concentration gradient [S21].
remedy: Have a pharmacology reviewer correct the text and spatial diagram; distinguish plasma/extracellular binding, concentration gradients, receptor unbinding and elimination.

title: Drug time runs at hidden 15x speed
evidence: dtMin=(dtSec/60)*15 and BIS smoothing uses dtSec*15, while EEG synthesis uses simTimeSec advanced by wall dtSec. The current module DOM has no speed control or 15x clock badge.
impact: Students can mislearn drug onset and lag. Drug transport, smoothing and displayed waveform time are not on one visible simulation clock.
remedy: Use one named clock with real and simulated time, visible speed and pause controls, and feed the same simulation time to PK, PD, waveforms and event records.
basis: Source inspection plus current local DOM

title: Publishing bypasses the clinical sanity checks
evidence: The deployment workflow runs npm ci and npm run build, then publishes. It does not run npm run sanity, validate reviewer status or detect generated review-document drift.
impact: A type-correct change can publish a physiological regression. Local green checks from a previous change are not a release gate.
remedy: Gate publication on numerical/regression tests, claim consistency, explicit release identity and review status appropriate to the changed module; preserve preview deployment for unreviewed work.

title: Valve faults change the capnogram without changing the flow network
evidence: Both stuck-valve probes produce identical Vt, Paw and flow to baseline. The flags add inspired CO2 using constants; visual ribbons reverse separately. They do not alter the pressure-flow solve.
impact: The diagram looks causal, but reverse circuit flow is not responsible for the resulting CO2. This restricts interpretation of combined faults and quantitative comparisons.
remedy: Use directional valve resistances in a shared gas-transport network, or present these as explicitly scripted pattern-recognition examples.

title: The curare cleft is drawn without a spontaneous effort
evidence: The fault subtracts a sine-shaped notch from capnogram target during a fixed phase. The mechanics probe is unchanged from the fully controlled case.
impact: It demonstrates a waveform label, not the coupled effect of a patient breathing against ventilation. The distinction matters for interpreting causes.
remedy: Inject a patient-effort signal into pressure/flow and transport its effect to the capnogram, or label the notch as an isolated waveform illustration.

title: The finite breathing gas reservoir never runs out mechanically
evidence: With an electrically driven piston and zero fresh gas for 30 minutes, the headless model still delivers 478 mL every breath, FiO2 is clamped to 2%, and bag fill remains 0.3. No finite reservoir depletion is solved. Zero inflow can also result from a supply fault with air off; the normal O2 stepper itself has a 0.2 minimum.
impact: This is outside the validity of the fixed-volume mixing assumption. The low-FiO2 alarm exists, but the breathing circuit still behaves as an inexhaustible reservoir.
remedy: Track total gas volume and reservoir collapse/air entrainment according to the chosen device topology, including loss of supply and disconnection tests.

title: Six machine architectures share too much undifferentiated physics
evidence: The kernel switches a few features: bellows coupling, piston decoupling, leak fraction, turbine CPAP and bellows motion. Draw-over still uses the same circle gas/absorber model; the volume-reflector gas front is a visual interpolation.
impact: These are six schematic variants, not six verified device implementations. Naming a technology does not establish faithful internals.
remedy: Define a sourced topology and validity envelope for each architecture. Start with one well-documented workstation; expand after topology-specific fault and bench comparisons.

title: Choosing another volatile mainly changes the appearance in the workstation
evidence: The M1 worker parameter type contains dial percentage but no agent identity. Selecting the agent changes the scene and display data, so agent-specific uptake/solubility cannot enter that kernel. M3 has a different kinetic model.
impact: A user can mistake a visual agent change for an agent-specific physiological experiment.
remedy: Expose the limited purpose of M1 agent selection, or integrate one reviewed kinetic model shared with the volatile lesson.

title: Gas-flow visuals use requested supply rather than actual supply
evidence: updateFlowRibbons computes fresh flow from requested O2/air/N2O and adds 45 L/min for flush. It does not apply the worker's wall-supply failure or concentrator 10 L/min flush limit. Fresh argon is also set to zero there.
impact: The diagram can imply supply persists after a failure or exaggerate concentrator flush. The visual explanation can disagree with the numbers.
remedy: Publish actual flow and species composition for each circuit edge in the simulation snapshot. Render that data without independently reconstructing supply logic.

title: The 50 Hz worker is a nominal callback schedule, not verified real time
evidence: The worker advances exactly PHYSICS_DT*speed per 20 ms setInterval callback; it does not account for elapsed monotonic time or suspended/throttled execution. The crisis clock similarly advances a fixed 0.5*speed per callback.
impact: Under scheduling delay, simulated time falls behind wall time. This may be acceptable when declared, but LIVE 50 Hz is not proof of timing accuracy.
remedy: Decide whether hidden tabs pause or catch up, use a fixed-step accumulator and explicit simulated time, and measure clock error/jitter under load. Avoid huge uncontrolled catch-up steps.

title: Rendering performance determines pharmacology progression
evidence: M3, M4 and M5 integrate in requestAnimationFrame and clamp elapsed frame time to 0.05 seconds. At a sustained 10 fps they integrate only about half of elapsed wall time. Paused/background frames lose time by design.
impact: The same scenario can progress at different rates on different student devices, undermining democratized access and timing comparisons.
remedy: Move numerical integration to a clock independent of drawing, use bounded fixed substeps and documented pause behavior, and verify convergence across render rates and speed settings.

title: Raw EEG sampling rate and time axis vary with the display frame rate
evidence: One sample is appended each animation frame, and the plot displays the last 220 samples with equally spaced x coordinates. The raw signal includes a 22 Hz component. At 30 fps its Nyquist limit is 15 Hz, so it aliases; the buffer represents different time spans on different devices.
impact: A raw EEG lesson can show materially different frequency content for the same state. There is no calibrated horizontal axis to reveal this.
remedy: Generate EEG on a fixed, documented sample clock above the required bandwidth with anti-aliasing; plot against timestamps and show seconds and microvolts.

title: The displayed DSA is not a spectrum computed from the raw EEG
evidence: The 30-bin spectrum is assembled from Gaussian bands plus Math.random. The raw trace is independently synthesized from three sine waves. The DSA grid is updated on another wall-time interval.
impact: Raw EEG, spectral display and depth labels may look mutually confirming although they do not share a measured signal. This is a concept illustration, not an EEG instrument emulator.
remedy: Derive a spectrogram from a shared signal with a defined window, overlap, units and color scale, and compare expert-labeled real recordings. If teaching bands only, label that boundary clearly.

title: Two different BIS models coexist
evidence: ThreeCompartmentEngine predicts BIS using model-specific gammaLow/gammaHigh; synthesizeEegSpectrum recomputes an index using fixed exponent 1.65 and other heuristics. The probe at Ce~6 gives 20.54 versus raw displayed 23. The latter is what the UI smooths.
impact: Selecting a named PK-PD model does not guarantee its PD output is the displayed index. Source PD parameters and illustrative artifact behavior are blended.
remedy: Use one explicitly versioned PD path, keep artifact demonstrations separate and show uncertainty. Resolve the paper-equation/Table-3 gamma discrepancy against supplementary code before asserting full parity [S11].

title: The TCI controller and manual pump lesson are not validated pump implementations
evidence: stepTci uses a proportional-feedforward heuristic with numeric gains and a cap. The manual bolus is targetCe*V1*0.85, with clearance-derived step-down rates. The code admits these are simulator heuristics; the prominent lesson still uses clinical pump terminology and dose units.
impact: Reaching a target concentration eventually does not validate the infusion trajectory, induction dose or a commercial TCI algorithm.
remedy: Retain a conceptual controller only with a visible limitation; benchmark complete trajectories against an independently implemented reference and do not present heuristic rates as a clinical regimen.

title: Avatar/model validity and opioid state are inadequately constrained
evidence: The six-year-old avatar can be combined with all listed models; Minto uses a 30 kg lean-mass floor. Every avatar has opioidCoAdmin=true even when the remifentanil target is turned to zero. Some covariate equations remain from-memory.
impact: The app can compare models outside demonstrated domains without making the extrapolation visible, and the opioid-associated PK setting is not derived from the current remifentanil control.
remedy: Give each model an explicit eligible population, route/units, coadministration meaning and extrapolation policy. Provide reference cases across ages, sex and body size, not only the standard adult.

title: There is no common patient across the rooms
evidence: ModuleRouter passes locale and navigation, not shared physiological state. Circuit, volatile, TCI, NMJ, heart, DLT and crisis models have separate parameters, clocks and reset behavior.
impact: The current product is a collection of learning objects. It cannot support the claim that all machine, drug, airway and patient changes interact as one anesthesia simulation.
remedy: Keep independent lessons where educationally useful; for integrated scenarios define a small authoritative patient state, units, clock and explicit adapters, then validate the couplings rather than merging everything at once.

title: The NMJ time courses and PTC are hand-tuned mappings
evidence: Rocuronium and sugammadex use normalized reservoirs and fixed coefficients, not molar mass balance or a referenced PK-PD model. Twitch heights use clipped linear occupancy curves; PTC is calculated continuously from occupancy even before a tetanic test. Cooldown blocks a button rather than modeling post-tetanic facilitation.
impact: The module can teach qualitative monitoring concepts, but its seconds, dose-response and recurrence trajectories are not established quantitative drug predictions.
remedy: Define the teaching boundary, remove exact response-time implications until benchmarked, and use reviewed PK-PD/monitoring response datasets if quantitative behavior is required.

title: The ultrasound is an acoustic illustration, not calibrated scanner physics
evidence: A correct squared impedance reflection coefficient is combined with R*60, added wall echoes, a sixfold strong-reflector gain, analytic speckle and drawn reverberation terms. There is no calibrated transducer/RF acquisition chain or reference-image error analysis.
impact: Some physical mechanisms are represented, but a realistic-looking image is not evidence that anatomy recognition or needle visibility transfers to a scanner.
remedy: Use paired real/virtual images reviewed by regional anesthetists, calibrate depth and orientation first, and state what artifacts and acquisition behavior the renderer does and does not emulate.

title: Injected anesthetic teleports with the needle tip
evidence: Each frame assigns laCenter=tip.clone() and sizes one ellipsoid from the current volume slider. Moving the needle moves the entire prior injectate; reducing the slider removes it. No prior deposits, tissue planes or injection pressure are retained.
impact: The displayed spread does not represent injection history or hydrodissection, so it can teach an incorrect procedure mechanism.
remedy: Deposit fluid at injection events in world coordinates and model or illustrate reviewed compartment boundaries. Show volume/rate, retain prior deposits, and handle unsafe injection sites explicitly.

title: Loss of resistance is a tissue label and bar, without procedural force fidelity
evidence: Real vertebral intersections are combined with synthetic soft tissues and illustrative syringe resistance values. The interaction is a depth/angle stepper, with no tactile device, syringe compliance, pressure input or physical force feedback.
impact: This is useful for spatial understanding, but it cannot demonstrate that a learner can feel or safely perform an epidural. A browser alone does not reproduce that task.
remedy: Name it a trajectory/anatomy lesson. Validate a separate low-cost physical trainer or optional measured haptic interface for the motor skill; do not award procedural competence from the screen.

title: The default trajectory and readouts reveal the solution
evidence: On initialization/reset the app searches for a typical successful trajectory. The panel exposes exact flavum and epidural depths. These aids remain part of the ordinary experience rather than a staged assessment.
impact: The learner can advance to a supplied answer without interpreting landmarks, uncertainty or the loss-of-resistance cue.
remedy: Keep explicit demonstration mode, then offer faded guidance and a separate practice case with concealed answer depths, variable anatomy and reviewed feedback.

title: Real source meshes do not establish representative or complete anatomy
evidence: The asset pipeline uses reduced BodyParts3D meshes. Plexus, pleural dome and neuraxial soft tissues are schematic. The bronchoscope lumen is a capsule-based reconstruction from extracted centerlines; cuff dimensions/compliance include illustrative values. M7 describes one adult male standing specimen.
impact: Dataset provenance is real, but procedural landmarks, deformability, patient variability and instrument fit still need validation. The broad phrase real human anatomy hides those distinctions.
remedy: Maintain a structure-level provenance map and clinician-approved landmark measurements, normal variants and pathology cases. Visibly distinguish measured mesh, derived geometry and schematic additions.

title: Unanswered questions produce apparently healthy results
evidence: scoreTotal treats every missing answer as option zero. The headless probe returns ASA I and the lowest bands for RCRI, STOP-Bang, Apfel and ARISCAT. The UI preselects those options and displays a band immediately.
impact: Unknown information becomes negative findings, which is a poor habit to teach in assessment. This is especially problematic if a user enters a real patient despite the disclaimer.
remedy: Represent unknown separately, require completeness before a final band, and distinguish a fictional worked case from free scoring.

title: Fasting rules flatten meal type and regional differences
evidence: adultSolid is a single generic Solids=6 h rule. The definitions mix adult ASA-associated advice and pediatric ESAIC intervals; changing interface locale does not select a clinical fasting policy. The 2026 international consensus distinguishes large/fatty meals and notes institutional protocols [S12].
impact: A generic planner may imply one universal timing rule. The defect is missing scope and meal classification; it is not a recommendation to impose a blanket eight-hour rule everywhere.
remedy: Choose an explicit guideline/jurisdiction/version, healthy-elective eligibility and meal type; teach exceptions and institutional variation with a reviewer. Keep a planner for synthetic cases, not patient instructions.

title: The first-use flow is designed around exploring controls
evidence: M1 starts in sandbox, 75% transparency, labels off; the guide is closed unless remembered open. Home says every screen opens on its instructions, but ModuleGuidePanel intentionally defaults closed. There is no first student objective/prediction/feedback loop.
impact: Novices must discover the instrument and its educational purpose simultaneously. More modules increase confusion rather than learning power.
remedy: Start with a short task: predict what disconnect will change, run it, observe the right signals, explain the mechanism and repeat a transfer case. Offer sandbox after the first guided exercise.

title: The learning record does not substantiate competence
evidence: The located xAPI call records opening the debrief as practiced. The helper defaults success=true and completion=true. The printable debrief is a generic prompt sheet, not an event-based replay. M11 progress is explicitly self-declared.
impact: A source-linked library and progress ticks are useful, but they do not prove procedural performance, mastery or an accredited curriculum outcome.
remedy: Define observable objectives and formative rubrics, capture action/time/reasoning evidence and export a clearly labeled learner attempt. Preserve self-declared curriculum progress as a separate feature.

title: Source counts create more assurance than they establish
evidence: Of the 156 sourced entries, 68 belong to M11 reference/library summaries. Entries cover heterogeneous claims, sometimes from abstracts. The registry points mostly to files and groups of values, not executable constant-to-source assertions.
impact: 156 sourced is not 156 validated simulation behaviors. It is also not a count of independently reviewed sources. Remaining unverified model inputs affect some of the most ambitious modules.
remedy: Separate source checked, equation transcribed, code verified, externally validated and clinician reviewed. Link each material coefficient or rule to a versioned source passage and tests; keep illustrative choices explicit.

title: Offline copies can retain obsolete clinical content
evidence: The update toast is dismissible and checks hourly only while online. There is no content expiry or withdrawn-lesson mechanism. BUILD_ID combines package version 1.0.0 and date, so multiple builds on one day share the same displayed identity.
impact: A reported error or reviewed correction may be difficult to tie to an exact build, and an offline learner can keep outdated content indefinitely.
remedy: Use immutable commit/content identities, display last-review dates and offline status, and define a proportionate withdrawal/update policy for serious educational errors.

title: Small dense controls and canvases limit access
evidence: Many labels use 9–11 px styles, steppers are 28 px high and presets 20 px high, with multiple scroll regions and unlabeled 3D canvases. Some monitor canvases have text summaries, but interactive 3D concepts lack equivalent nonvisual tasks. The archived phone captures show stacked layouts, not proven usability.
impact: This conflicts with use on inexpensive phones, projectors and assistive technologies. This is a usability/accessibility concern, not a completed WCAG conformance audit.
remedy: Test keyboard, screen reader, zoom, contrast and touch tasks; use larger key controls, readable text and a non-3D schematic/text path for the same learning objective.

title: Arabic selection is not a complete Arabic clinical interface
evidence: The shell offers ar-MA and RTL, while most modules choose French whenever locale is not en-INT. M11 programme/library labels are largely French even in English mode.
impact: The language menu implies a degree of localization the clinical learning content does not provide. RTL French content can be harder to read.
remedy: Label language coverage honestly, separate region from language, and have a medical translator plus a clinician review Arabic terminology, numbers, reading direction and task comprehension.

title: The machine reads as a schematic prop rather than a coherent instrument
evidence: The workstation is procedural Three.js geometry. The historical workstation capture shows a large translucent slab, generic gauges/knobs, exposed floating lungs, cluttered overlap and mixed physical scales. The code explicitly scales the patient differently from the circuit. Mesh controls are not directly operated; settings live beside the scene.
impact: The viewer sees effort and technical detail, but has weak spatial hierarchy and little sense of operating a real workstation. This is an art-direction and interaction judgment, not proof that AI generated every object.
remedy: Build one dimensioned generic workstation from documented engineering references; use consistent real-world units, distinct material families, clear assembly, readable labels and click-to-inspect components. Use a separate schematic cutaway view when physical scale obscures a mechanism.
basis: Source inspection plus historical image review

title: The free/offline promise lacks a documented low-end device acceptance test
evidence: The production build passes but warns about large chunks: index 856.20 kB and three 552.00 kB before gzip. The PWA precache is 41 entries / 3619.38 KiB. M7 and M8 create additional WebGL views, and ultrasound computes slices on the main thread. Adaptive tiers exist, but there is no measured target-device report in the inspected test suite.
impact: Bundle size alone does not prove slow performance. The gap is evidence that cold start, heat, battery and task responsiveness work for the phones the mission targets.
remedy: Define a representative low-end Android, mid-range device and desktop test matrix; measure loading, sustained frame/physics rates, interactions and offline recovery. Keep numerical behavior invariant when visual quality drops.
basis: Observed build output; source inspection; device validation gap

title: The dependency audit has three moderate findings
evidence: npm audit reports moderate findings for glob, minimatch and workbox-build; no high or critical findings. They are transitive build-tool findings. Full advisory paths and suggested fixes are preserved in dependency-audit.json.
impact: This is maintenance work, not evidence of an exploitable deployed patient-data service. The static app and build pipeline have different exposure.
remedy: Review the actual advisories, update compatible build dependencies in an isolated change and rerun build, PWA/offline and simulator checks. Do not apply a blind force update.
basis: Live npm registry audit, saved JSON
